title: TTL and session-owned retention semantics
desc: Use a controlled clock to check TTL expiry, explicit release, and while-in-use ownership without a wall-clock expiry. Unavailable results report expired/released status; cancelling completed fetches leaves their published lease active.

title: Transfer limits and managed artifact paths
desc: Check positive safe-integer aggregate limits, known-size rejection, MIME parameters, and sanitized filenames. Managed output paths stay inside the owning account folder and unknown-length transfers stop at the configured aggregate ceiling.

title: On-demand MIME selection and transforms
desc: Validate raw-message, body, attachment, and selected-part requests against MIME structure, including the supplied multipart fixture. Check body preferences, inline resources, and optional Markdown only where those capabilities are implemented.

title: Revision precedence and fenced acknowledgements
desc: Exercise newer, equal, and older source revisions plus stale batch owners. Only strictly newer rows change analytical values; acknowledging a claimed revision cannot clear a newer pending revision.

title: Deterministic CSV and JSON rendering
desc: Check escaping, Unicode, nulls, timestamps, supported value encodings, and requested projections. Ordering includes stable logical-key or dimension tie-breakers so unchanged results produce identical export bytes.

title: Stable canonical UTC dates
desc: Exercise INTERNALDATE, unambiguous Date header, and first-fetch fallback precedence across timezone and month boundaries. Refreshes preserve the first chosen date, provenance, and partition.

title: Durable message identity
desc: Check account/mailbox/UIDVALIDITY/UID identity, UUID encoding, and lossless decimal Gmail IDs. Sequence numbers never become durable keys; Gmail correlation never replaces mailbox fetch identity.

title: Header and MIME metadata derivation
desc: Use valid and malformed header/MIME fixtures to check flags, addresses, sender domains, attachment counts, thread depth, and delay calculations against the documented derivations. Unspecified decoding and classification policies need explicit expectations before implementation.

title: Core and extension schema conversion
desc: Check core field types, null handling, and JSON extensions conversion to Parquet MAP values containing canonical JSON. Reject incompatible representations without silently dropping or changing values.

title: Official outcomes and terminal job states
desc: Check succeeded, retry, failed, and skipped outcomes independently of custom diagnostics. Required failures or skipped required steps prevent success; optional permanent failures yield warnings only after every instantiated step is terminal.

title: Typed transformer input and output encoding
desc: Round-trip JSON, binary, UTF-8, and no-output contracts through typed transformers and their erased wrappers. Every transformer receives immutable normalized metadata and declared dependency outputs with a stable idempotency key.

title: Pipeline graph validation and readiness
desc: Reject dependency cycles, duplicate step IDs, and repeated transformer names within a pipeline. Ready steps require stable prerequisites; optional predecessors without output require an explicit supported input contract.

title: Transformer registry and version validation
desc: Reject empty or untrimmed names, duplicate registrations, invalid Int32 versions, and missing or incompatible transformer contracts. Verify synchronous adapters and type erasure retain declared names, versions, and output schemas.

title: Retry classification and bounded backoff
desc: Use a controlled clock and jitter source to check persisted attempts, retry deadlines, exhaustion, and infrastructure error classification. Custom status values never control scheduling.

title: Compatible reuse and self-contained outputs
desc: Check every reuse key and output schema compatibility, rejecting stale fingerprints or invalid artifacts. A reused result retains an audit link and its own usable output; completed valid work does not need execution again.

title: Grouping statistics and relationship rules
desc: Check grouped projections, count/statistics modes, having/order scopes, alias collisions, quantile bounds, and allow-listed aggregates. Relationship names remain in their fixed namespace; one-to-many aggregates require explicit supported configuration.

title: Allow-listed identifiers and typed bindings
desc: Validate dataset fields, expression scopes, variable types, array sizes, and timezone-bearing timestamp conversion. Reject SQL, paths, or URLs supplied as query structure and reject unknown identifiers or unbound variables; hostile text inside allowed scalar/array values remains separate bound data.

title: Query request and expression parsing
desc: Accept documented request modes and literal-free operators/functions with source spans. Reject duplicate or unknown JSON keys, conflicting modes, malformed collections, expression literals, and excessive configured token/depth limits.

title: Deterministic period plans and archive eligibility
desc: Check UTC ranges, task identities, stage dependencies, and complete closed-month eligibility using a controlled clock. Open months and partial or multi-month plans omit archive stages and can complete after projection verification.

title: Idempotent task keys and range coverage
desc: Check deterministic task keys across page replay and independent account/mailbox generations. Period coverage is keyed by UTC range and generation; the highest observed UID alone never proves another date range complete.

title: Credential and provider authentication boundaries
desc: Use scripted IMAP providers for PLAIN XOAUTH2 OAUTHBEARER and SCRAM-SHA-256. Reject empty multiple and malformed mechanism selections unsupported capabilities invalid TLS and bad credentials. Replace expired tokens through the API; reconnect uses new credentials and no secret appears in SQLite files logs events or exports.

title: Account isolation and persistent configuration
desc: Configure two accounts with overlapping mailbox UIDs, then sync, process, query, and reopen their stores. Non-secret settings persist in shared SQLite while rows, DuckDB files, archives, and temporary artifacts stay scoped to the owning account.

title: Exclusive process writer ownership
desc: Open a temporary library root from competing processes and verify only one owns the operational store for its lifetime. Release after shutdown or termination permits recovery; workers alone cannot authorize a second process writer.

title: Lease cleanup across sessions and completed cancellations
desc: Publish TTL and while-in-use content, restart or shut down its owner session, and run cleanup. TTL expiry and session release remove only eligible artifacts; active leases retain access, released/expired results fail deterministically, and cancelling completed fetches does not release their result.

title: Explicit content downloads and atomic artifact publication
desc: Confirm metadata synchronization requests headers/structure without body bytes, then explicitly fetch supported complete or selective MIME content from a scripted server. Persist selection/transform options across restart; check aggregate streaming limits, cancellation, safe paths, complete publication, and abandoned partial cleanup.

title: Store migration and dependency-safe pruning
desc: Once explicit migration and retention policies exist, reopen historical fixtures and prune eligible history/artifacts. Preserve latest identity/date checkpoints, referenced immutable inputs, and valid reusable outputs; incompatible stores require the chosen explicit migration or rejection path.

title: Portable Rust and embedded engine
desc: After pinning targets and adapters compile and link the Rust core and C ABI on supported Linux Windows and macOS targets. Exercise SQLite DuckDB and Parquet without Apple frameworks or OS credential stores.

title: Atomic results and period completion gates
desc: Inject failure around result saves and required/optional outcomes, including work still running. Step state and complete output commit together; terminal jobs have no unfinished steps, required failure blocks period export, and warning-success proceeds only after all included jobs satisfy the gate.

title: Resume compatibility and result reuse
desc: Reopen pending jobs with missing or version/schema-mismatched registrations and confirm blocking occurs before an attempt is claimed. Compatible prior results are copied with valid output and audit identity; incompatible inputs or schemas execute only through an explicit supported new contract.

title: Persisted metadata snapshots and artifact integrity
desc: Persist normalized input envelopes before scheduling and restart before execution. Transformers receive the same verified schema, revision, locator, fingerprint, and metadata; missing or corrupt inputs fail through the documented contract instead of using mutable current metadata.

title: Read-only queries resource limits and deterministic exports
desc: Submit hostile inputs and exceed configured query/time/result limits, then cancel active execution. Stable sanitized errors include relevant spans without raw SQL/bindings; storage remains unchanged, and repeated scoped CSV/JSON exports are identical without fetching message bodies.

title: Execute the query catalogue and supplied examples
desc: Run all six supplied requests against a seeded real DuckDB/Parquet dataset, plus rows, count, statistics, and supported relationship cases. Check expected grouping, timestamp binding, null behavior, and aggregate results with documented tolerances for approximate statistics.

title: Correction compaction and reader-safe generations
desc: Update an archived month while archive/compaction work and readers are active. Replacement contains the prior full partition plus fixed overlay revisions, retains concurrent newer corrections, commits exactly one current immutable generation, and keeps retired files until their readers release them.

title: Archive publication and manifest crash boundaries
desc: Inject failures at claim, write, verification, atomic publication, and manifest/staging commit boundaries, then reopen. Invalid files never become current; published files are reverified before finalization, and failed or interrupted batches retain recoverable queryable rows.

title: Queryable archive snapshots and schema parity
desc: Archive a complete closed month for both datasets while querying before, during, and after publication. Live and exporting snapshots remain visible without duplicates; separate manifests, counts, paths, and schema versions agree with verified Parquet types and extension values.

title: Lease expiry and concurrent correction fencing
desc: Expire or replace an export claim while its executor is suspended, then accept a newer correction before the old acknowledgement. Batch and claimed-version fencing reject stale completion/failure updates and leave the newer revision exportable.

title: Dual-store projection crash recovery
desc: Project both metadata and processing results, interrupt after DuckDB commit but before SQLite acknowledgement, then reclaim and replay. Equal/newer destination rows are successful no-ops; all claimed snapshots are acknowledged without losing pending changes.

title: Monotonic revisions across jobs and restarts
desc: Accept older and newer job inputs, finish them in reverse order, and restart between allocations. The shared durable sequence never resets per job or account; late older outputs cannot overwrite newer analytical state or correction revisions.

title: Latest-revision deduplication before deletions
desc: Place conflicting revisions and tombstones for metadata and processing keys across live, exporting, archive, and overlay sources. Queries choose the newest revision before filtering deletions, so stale rows never resurrect deleted messages or results.

title: Serialized DuckDB writes and transactional failures
desc: Suspend exporters across worker suspension points and contend with metadata writers, migration, and archival. Schema preparation precedes claims; a bad row rolls back the full batch, supported batch splitting isolates it, and failure-record save errors preserve the primary error while releasing the writer gate.

title: Cancellation resume and replay-safe progress
desc: Cancel an active run, await cooperative stopping, then resume and subscribe to status/events. Completed work remains reusable, initial snapshots and events are ordered, and counters reconcile without double-counting replayed tasks or exposing content/secrets.

title: Atomic discovery pages and bounded fan-out
desc: Interrupt before and after the SQLite save that commits a page cursor and child tasks, then resume against a scripted IMAP server. No UIDs disappear or duplicate work; children from committed pages drain under bounded backpressure without waiting for all discovery to finish.

title: Date-range refresh and mailbox generation changes
desc: Sync overlapping and disjoint UTC ranges with changed flags, new messages, moves, expunges, and a changed UIDVALIDITY. Candidate searches are filtered by canonical dates; range coverage and generation reconciliation neither skip messages nor confuse old UIDs with new identities.

title: Restart with retries and preserved completed work
desc: Terminate during fetch, transformation, and retry waiting, reopen the persisted stores, and resume. Attempts, deadlines, input identities, and completed work survive; ambiguous external effects use the persisted idempotency key and reconciliation contract before retry.

title: Bounded scheduler concurrency and durable claims
desc: Run multiple messages and dependent steps with suspended executors. Enforce independent configured message/step limits, preserve dependency ordering, and prevent duplicate execution through durable claims; reclaim expired leases while fencing late results.

title: ABI JSON and handle validation
desc: Check ABI versioning closed and stale handles malformed UTF-8 unknown methods schema versions size limits lossless integer encodings and authentication redaction.

title: Stateful session and C buffer ownership
desc: Exercise open multiple calls concurrent polling auth replacement cancellation and close through a C consumer. Free each returned buffer once; verify connection reuse deterministic close root ownership and restart with durable checkpoints but no credentials.

title: SQL migrations and constraints
desc: Reopen supported schema versions and inject migration and transaction failures. Check foreign keys unique identities revision allocation rollback busy limits and account-scoped snapshots.
